instruction: Explain what is meant by the 'bias-variance trade-off'.
output: The bias-variance trade-off is an important concept in machine learning which states that a model’s accuracy is determined by both the bias and the variance of the model. A model with high bias, or underfitting, will have low accuracy, while a model with high variance, or overfitting, will also have low accuracy. The ideal model is the one which has low bias and low variance, but this is a difficult balance to achieve. This is essentially a trade-off between two conflicting goals, where reducing the bias can cause an increase in the variance, and vice versa. In order to achieve the best model, it is important to strike the right balance between bias and variance.

instruction: Compare and contrast horror movies from the 70s to ones made today.

They tended to be more psychological in nature, so the protagonist would face an unseen danger that the audience had to imagine but never see. Movies today tend to be faster-paced, relying more on jump scares and special effects that show explicit horror. While modern movies still have psychological elements, they tend to be more explicit in how they depict the horror, often showing what is causing the terror in graphic detail. Furthermore, modern horror movies tend to be more focused on the protagonists surviving the physical danger they face.

An artificial neuron is an algorithm that simulates the behavior of a biological neuron. It can also be trained with a learning algorithm to adjust its weights according to external inputs. Artificial neurons are used in neural networks and deep learning algorithms.
